chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi from Sa'd ibn Sa'd said: I asked him, meaning Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

About a man who had a son whom he claimed (as his own), but he disowned him and excluded him from the inheritance, and I was his executor (wasi). What should I do? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The son remains [entitled] due to his declaration in the court; the executor does not remove him regarding anything that he has knowledge of.'

key_terms.لِإِقْرَارِهِ بِالْمَشْهَدِ: Due to his declaration/testimony in court

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a disowned son's inheritance share when an executor manages the estate?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that a son’s legal status is established by his own testimony or acknowledgment (*iqrar*) rather than solely by the father's unilateral disownment (*tanfid*). The executor (*wasi*) cannot withhold the son's inheritance share if he is aware of this established fact, emphasizing the principle that judicial or witnessed recognition overrides private paternal declaration in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the importance of objective evidence in estate distribution, ensuring the son's rights are preserved against arbitrary exclusion by the estate manager.
